title: Adding a "How to contribute an example" site on development
body:
This is adding a new site in the 'development' section of the documentation. It includes information on how to contribute an example to the website.
!!!Please add your comments/suggestions/tips to this, it might still miss some important information!!!
(I assigned a lot of people, I hope you can add your important experience on this)
I will also go over this with Auguste when he tries to move an example


# Checklist: `x` (done) or `~` (irrelevant)

- [ ] [I am familiar with **ASE's contribution guidelines.**](https://ase-lib.org/development/contribute.html)
- [ ] [**Doc strings** in code changed in this MR are up to date.](https://ase-lib.org/development/python_codingstandard.html#writing-documentation-in-the-code)
- [ ] [**Unit tests** have been added for new or changed code.](https://ase-lib.org/development/tests.html)
- [ ] [**Changes** have been added in `changelog.d` using `scriv`.](https://ase-lib.org/development/writing_changelog.html)
- [x] [**Issue is resolved** via "closes #1804 " if applicable.](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/issues/managing_issues.html#closing-issues-automatically)
author: HannaTuerk

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body:
I think the section titles "introduction" and "learning outcomes" are reversed here. Usually "learning outcomes" refers to a high-level summary of what will be learned - like the "overview" section in the 2023 tutorial pages https://ase-workshop-2023.github.io/tutorial/02-the-atoms-object/index.html. That seems aligned with this UNESCO definition: https://uis.unesco.org/en/glossary-term/learning-outcomes

Whereas in academic writing an "introduction" usually includes a bit of context and external references.

comments.author: HannaTuerk
comments.body: ok good point, I'll change this

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags that section titles 'introduction' and 'learning outcomes' are reversed and should be swapped.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body:
```suggestion:-9+0
- a python environment with relevant packages installed. These are defined in the ase "docs" dependency group and can be installed with

.. code-block:: console

    $ pip install ase[docs]
```

I don't like to include `--user` in documentation these days, because it is quite common now that people are using some kind of environment management. In that case `--user` installs can make things a lot more messy; you end up with things in `~/.local/bin` that refer to python interpreters you might have deleted, etc.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests removing --user flag from pip install command with explanation and provides replacement code.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
You can use the `:git:` role instead of linking to files in git:

```
examples in the :git:`examples` folder
```

Also probably split into two sentences "....folder.  These are rendered...."

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests using the :git: role instead of a direct link, and recommends splitting into two sentences.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: should we recommend an editable installation (something like `pip install --editable example/path/to/ase[docs]`)?  Otherwise I think it might install a non-editable version as the importable one.

comments.author: HannaTuerk
comments.body:
good question, I think in general this is not necessary when one builds the documentation locally (at least I did not have any problems with a regular install). But it could be desirable in case one develops code and changes the documentation at the same time, but this is more advanced and then I would think that people doing this would know that they can install the repo in editable format.
I would keep it the way it is, unless you really want the `--editable`

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: I agree to keep it simple. Editable install is not always better and can make it more difficult to figure out what is going on.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests recommending an editable installation to avoid issues with the importable version.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: In order to pass CI, a commit must pass `ruff check` and `ruff format`.  So I think we should say directly "please install ruff" instead of thinking of it as an example

comments.author: HannaTuerk
comments.body: ok sure, I added to explicitly ask for ruff and so it includes the commands that need to be passed. In the ASE contribute page, just a linter is requested, we could in general also refer to ruff there

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests changing the documentation to directly instruct users to install ruff rather than treating it as an example.
